title: Log-domain and projected Schur cutoff stress
question: Can log-domain Gibbs likelihoods and explicit projection off the sqrt(pi) constant mode extend the R-415 Schur stress to larger cutoffs without mistaking floating-point zero-mode drift for graph disconnection?
method: Reconstruct coordinate Gibbs masses with log-sum-exp over energy eigenvectors and form ordered conditional rows from log-marginals.
Build the normalized intrinsic momentum graph and compute its positive spectrum on the orthogonal complement of the exact sqrt(pi) constant mode.
Recompute the R-406 harmonic coarse/residual gaps and check the conservative Schur gap below the projected positive gap on 13 volume-two cutoffs, three beta values and both orientations.
Repeat the full grid in an independent plain-loop implementation and run hostile mutations for raw zero drift, wrong projection, naive underflow, weight rescaling and nonpositive rows.
Compile Lean R416 for scalar positivity, projection nonnegativity, Schur positivity and finite-scope bookkeeping.
finding: The primary lane passes 4370/4370 assertions, the independent lane passes 4370/4370, the hostile lane passes 9/9, the integrated verifier passes 39/39, and Lean R416 compiles over 13 cutoffs, 78 profiles and 1410 conditional rows. Primary projected gaps are [0.6867237745188259,11.524804493011532] and Schur gaps are [0.3476008247075759,5.985995817095592]. Raw zero-mode residual reaches 1.0782998803365607 in the primary lane and 1.1256888563326983 independently, while projected gaps remain positive; direct underflow rows are zero and common weight scaling has residual 0.0.
decision_reason: The log-domain and exact-constant-mode projection remove a diagnosed numerical ambiguity in the high-cutoff stress and make the R-406 Schur target auditable without treating a drifting raw zero eigenvalue as a physical or graph disconnection. The finite route advances the interface toward an analytic common-core estimate, while cutoff/volume/source/phase/exhaustion uniformity and every QFT promotion premise remain open.

adversarial_review.check: At high cutoff the raw zero residual exceeds the declared diagnostic threshold, but the exact-constant-mode projected gap remains positive.
Projecting away from the wrong vector gives a negative minimum -38.090756543305964.
Naive exponential formation underflows in two hostile entries while log-sum-exp remains finite.
Common weight scaling has residual 0.0 and a nonpositive conditional row is rejected.
Finite positive projected and Schur gaps do not imply common-core, regulator-independent, QFT or physical-sector closure.

qft_interface.closed: Finite log-domain Gibbs reconstruction, projected positive graph spectrum, Schur coarse/residual stress, increasing-cutoff table, independent and hostile checks, and Lean scalar bookkeeping.
qft_interface.open: Analytic positive-measure and conditional-marginal estimates on one Hamiltonian common core; cutoff, volume, source, phase and exhaustion uniformity; R-415/R-399 transfer; OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction; continuum and physical mass-gap obligations.

next_action: Prove an analytic positive-measure and conditional-marginal estimate controlling both Schur components uniformly on one Hamiltonian common core, then transfer the bound to the R-415 proper-time budget. If a validated growing stress produces a genuine projected or Schur collapse, retain the finite table and record the route-local obstruction without promotion.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite log-domain/projected-Schur cutoff stress only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform gap, common core, phase selection, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: Projection and log-domain reconstruction remove a diagnosed floating-point failure mode and extend the finite stress; they do not turn finite numerical persistence into regulator-independent coercivity.
